questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, slows reaction time, and reduces coordination.

questions.question: On a slippery road, maintain a following distance that is:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on slippery roads. Keep a longer following distance when driving on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces vision clarity, makes you less alert, and worsens judgment. You will have trouble judging distances and speeds.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs affect many driving skills. They slow reaction time, reduce coordination, decrease alertness, and harm concentration.

questions.question: Before making a turnabout, drivers should:

options.text: Honk to alert other drivers to their intentions.
Be sure their vehicle is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
Come to a complete stop in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure their vehicle is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
questions.explanation: A turnabout is a legal way to turn around. Make sure your car can be seen for at least 500 feet in both directions before starting.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: With a green light, you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a steady green signal.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at collisions or unusual events causes traffic congestion and should be avoided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead.

questions.question: Night driving is difficult because:

options.text: The speed limit is increased at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
Distance and vehicle speed are hard to judge in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distance and vehicle speed are hard to judge in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder due to low visibility. You can only see as far as your headlights reach. This makes it hard to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are traveling.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are greeting another driver.
When it can help prevent a crash.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it can help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Other drivers may not see you unless they are looking your way. Use your horn to get their attention in a dangerous situation. This can help prevent a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers about traffic laws. It means you cannot turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicles block the rear view of large trucks and buses.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not have enough time to stop and could hit you.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection if it is safe and clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can proceed. First, yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection. Then go through when it is clear.

questions.question: If you are feeling tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio.
Park in a safe area and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in a safe area and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you cannot keep your eyes open, drift out of your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired. Find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers of a school zone. This sign tells you that children or other pedestrians may be nearby.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe on the highway?

options.text: Slower traffic stays to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, do not back up or make a U-turn. Go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and force other vehicles to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes, check for vehicles behind and to the side of you. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Hold the wheel steady and take your foot off the gas to let the vehicle slow down. Gently apply the brakes when it is safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed a lot.

questions.question: You should drive at the maximum speed limit only:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
Under perfect conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under perfect conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally go when conditions are perfect. Drive at the speed of other traffic, up to the limit. Always drive at a safe speed.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Always check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This makes sure it is safe to move into the other lane.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even if there is no marked crosswalk. Pedestrians have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. These include prescription drugs like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter medicines like cough syrup and cold tablets, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you may fall asleep while driving. This can cause a serious crash that injures or kills you or others.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. This helps you see vehicles in the lane you want to enter and keeps you from hitting other drivers.

questions.question: When may you pass a vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to pass. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see what is around you. This helps you stop safely without hitting other vehicles.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Increase your speed.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look to the rear and both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to make the turn safely.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.
Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor decisions while driving.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross them to pass. Traffic from either direction cannot pass on this type of road.
